speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are presenting with right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To determine the underlying cause, have you noticed any changes in your handwriting, vision, or muscle stiffness in the past year?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis. The acute onset of psychiatric symptoms (paranoia, agitation), cognitive decline (forgetfulness), and new-onset focal motor deficits (right leg weakness) in a young male is highly suggestive of this paraneoplastic syndrome, often associated with an ovarian teratoma. I am requesting an MRI of the brain and a serum test for Anti-NMDA receptor antibodies to confirm.
